memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then the Lord said to Moses, "Tell Aaron, 'Stretch out your staff and strike the dust of the ground,' and throughout the land of Egypt the dust will become gnats." They did this, and when Aaron stretched out his hand with the staff and struck the dust of the ground, gnats came on people and animals. All the dust throughout the land of Egypt became gnats." - Exodus 8:16-17 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Notice something different about this plague: there is no warning. The first two came with an announcement and an opportunity to relent. This one simply falls.

Pharaoh had received his warnings and dismissed them. There is a point at which God stops repeating Himself. That should sober us. God's patience is enormous, but it is not the same thing as endless permission.

Notice also what God uses. Dust. The cheapest, most worthless substance in Egypt — the thing under everyone's feet. Egypt's magnificent civilisation is brought to misery by dust.

God delights in using what the world despises. Paul says God chose the foolish, the weak, and the lowly things of this world so that no one may boast before Him (1 Cor 1:27-29).

If you have ever felt like dust — overlooked, ordinary, of no particular account — remember that dust is exactly the material God has always liked working with. He made the first human from it.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Have I been treating God's patience as permission to delay?
2. Do I believe God can use someone as ordinary as me?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, I am dust, and You know it. Take my ordinary life and use it for Your purposes. Amen.
